%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for 9mm pistols and submachine guns. An effective sound suppressor for calibre 9mm weapons. It is very archaic and yet quite effective. Its body contains a tightly-packed roll of fine brass mesh. The front of the unit comprises a set of rubber wipes with calibre-sized holes for the bullet to pass through. Normally used for close-combat engagements against lightly-armoured enemies and for assassinations.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]very high

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 5.56x45mm and 7.62x39mm weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for the AK-100 series of rifles. The ATG (Автоматный Тактический Глушитель - "Tactical Assault Rifle Suppressor") is a modernized form of the PBS-1.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 9x19mm and .45 calibre weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for sevral modern handguns and SMGs. Designed to be durable and compact, this American-made aluminum device can be used "wet" or "dry" (with or without lubricants). It was originally designed by a military request for a small but effective suppressor for the M1911A1. Since then, it has found a place among Stalkers, for whom reliability and low weight are king.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]high

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 7.62mm weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for the SVD sniper rifle. "KZRZP" is a designation of Russian-built suppressors. This model was specifically constructed with the SVD in mind, although a standard SVD does not have the correct threading from the factory, so it must be re-threaded. It can also be used on other 7.62mm rifles after their barrels have been also threaded to accept it.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 5.56x45mm and 7.62x51mm weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for standard NATO rifles. Without any serial number, this model has likely been produced by or for the Mercenaries. It is quite a versatile device with a simple and durable design.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]high

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 7.62mm, 9mm and 12-gauge weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for the older AK models, such as the AKM and AK-47, as well as the 9mm Kalashnikov SMGs and the 12ga. Kalashnikov shotguns. It was introduced in the 1960s for use mostly among Spetsnaz and KGB, and saw widespread use in the Soviet-Afghan War of the 1980s. It is composed of two parts: a wider rubber wipe section in the back, and a narrower baffle section in the front. The former seems to have not been replaced in a long time. In fact, the tediousness of replacing the wipes is what lead to the development of the VSS and AS Val integrally silenced rifles.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 5.45x39mm weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for AKS-74U rifle. It was often issued with the AKS-74UB special variant alongside subsonic rounds.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 5.45x39mm weapons
 
%c[ui_gray_1]Suppressor for AK-74 rifles and RPK-74 machine guns. It was created in the mid-1980s due to a lack of a suppressor design for the 5.45x39mm round.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium
